newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian credit seen picking up, money to be scarce.
newsitem.headline: Indian credit seen picking up, money to be scarce.

text.p: The Indian demand for credit is picking up, the chairman of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI), one of India's leading long-term lending institutions said on Thursday.

"With the reduction in cash reserve ratio requirements and relatively modest government borrowing in the first part of the year, the liquidity position is showing signs of easing," ICICI chairman Narayanan Vaghul said in a speech read out in his absence at the firm's annual general meeting.

"However, with demand for credit picking up and large projected government borrowings during the year, a scenario of capital scarcity appears likely to continue in the medium term," Vaghul told ICICI's shareholders.

"The extent to which this would affect industrial growth rates would depend on the ability of corporates to raise capital in international markets to supplement the domestic availability and improvement in productivity," he said.
Vaghul said the slow pace of growth in infrastructure and the continuing poor performance of the domestic equity markets were areas of concern.

"On an overall analysis, however, the economy appears to be moving in the right direction with increased focus on globalisation and looks set to achieve the growth rate benchmarks now established," Vaghul said.
